snippet.title: Friends shocked to learn Princess Diana is dead (1997 video)
snippet.description:
Historic event - The unexpected death of Princess Diana.
Friends playing cards learn that Princess Diana was injured in a car accident, then react when TV news says she has died.  I recorded this home video in 1997 and it sat in a box for 20+ years.  This is the full, unedited version as I recorded it that night, from the original videotape.  The cuts between shots are when I paused the camera at the time.  

To answer some questions that have popped up -   I recorded this home video in 1997 the night Diana died and it sat in a box for 20+ years, when I thought maybe it would be interesting enough to share on YouTube.  Why was I recording?  I was trying out a new camcorder by recording friends playing the card game UNO, laughing and joking around.  When my mom called me to say "Turn on the tv, Diana was in a car crash" we kept our game going while monitoring the text on the bottom of the TV screen.   When the screen text changed to "Diana dead" the true reality of the situation hit like a ton of bricks and we stopped playing UNO of course (and stopped joking) and rushed over to the TV.   This was recorded in America, in the state of Iowa.  All of the guys in the video are still alive today (as of September 18, 2026).  The guy who screams when he learns Diana has died is my friend Ken.  It is his genuine reaction to the news of Diana's death.  Some people call it a "Wilhelm scream."   (Apparently that's a movie term).   The guy who stifles a smile after Ken's scream is Scott.  (Scott's brief smile is a reaction to Ken's loud silly scream, NOT to Diana's death).   When CNN announced that Diana had died I didn't turn the camera back to the TV because my immediate instinct was that it would be more interesting to capture my friends' reactions.   Some people call this video the first of what are now called "reaction" videos, a term that didn't exist in 1997 (and neither did YouTube, which began in 2005).  People have asked me what model camcorder and what format videotape this was recorded on, and unfortunately I don't recall.  (I have now found out which model....see below)   I had several camcorders over the years.  All I know it was an RCA model because I have still photos of me using it and the letters RCA can be seen in red on the camera's strap.  The camcorder also had an unusual feature.  A button would allow for "fade to black" OR "fade to white."  I've never seen fade to white on any other camcorder but as I was using it to record this video at the time it occurred to me that I should use fade to white when I finished.  It would give a more "heavenly" feel.   (UPDATE ON THE CAMCORDER MODEL:  Thanks to a commenter I have learned that the camera was RCA CC634 Model LCD Small Wonder, which used the VHS-C format tapes.  It is one of only four RCA camcorder models which featured the "fade to white" button as well as the "fade to black."   I identified it by going to google images and searching those 4 models he suggested it might be.)

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Performed “Dirty Diana” for Princess Diana 💖
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson meeting Princess Diana backstage at Wembley in 1988 became one of the most memorable stories from the Bad Tour. Before the show, Michael had removed “Dirty Diana” from the setlist out of respect for Princess Diana, but after she told him it was her favorite song, he ended up performing it that night. A legendary Michael Jackson and Princess Diana moment from Live at Wembley that fans still talk about today. Source

Source: Michael Jackson’s Private Home Movies

snippet.description:
Hello everyone!

In this small video we see how Michael Jackson, the king of Pop, misses the princess of England.

Diana was a good friend of MJ and her death gave Michael a deep trauma. After her death he tough that we was the one to go next. Little that he know that unfortunately, he too would leave us too soon.

I want to take this moment to thank them both, for being amazing human beings, and shining a light in this dark and cruel world.

Wherever you both are, just know that everyone on earth misses you! Thank you Michael Jackson and thank you Princess Diana.

While performing in front of tens of thousands, a young fan rushed onto the stage and hugged him tightly. Instead of pushing her away, Michael comforted her while continuing to sing, showing his warmth and humanity. After the moment ended, Michael broke down in tears on stage, leaving the audience deeply moved. snippet.title: Michael Jackson on Princess Diana’s Death | His 1997 Tribute | 29th Anniversary
snippet.description:
On 31 August 1997, the world lost Princess Diana.

Days later, Michael Jackson sat down with Barbara Walters and spoke about hearing the news — how he collapsed in grief, cancelled a concert, and later dedicated a performance to her.

“I love you, Diana. Shine and shine on forever. You are the true princess of the people.”

Today marks 29 years since her passing.

Michael Jackson and Princess Diana met in 1988 at Wembley Stadium during the Bad Tour. Both lived under intense public and media scrutiny. After her death, Jackson called it one of the great tragedies of the time and honoured her on stage with Smile and Gone Too Soon.

Remembering Princess Diana

1 July 1961 – 31 August 1997
Clip: Barbara Walters / 20/20 interview, September 1997.
